title_original: Abdallah Al-Khatib’s ‘Chronicles From The Siege’ pulled by producer from Marrakech festival competition
excerpt_original: Al-Khatib has strongly opposed the decision to withdraw his film, which was pulled at last minute by rights holder Issaad Film Productions.

blocks.text: Source: Issaad Film Production
‘Chronicles From The Siege’

Palestinian-Syrian filmmaker Abdallah Al-Khatib’s Chronicles From The Siege has been withdrawn at the last minute from the official competition of the Marrakech International Film Festival, due to start in Morocco on November 20.
The film, which won the best first feature award in the Berlinale’s Perspectives section earlier this year, was withdrawn by Algerian production company and rights holder Issaad Film Productions.

Marrakech organisers said Al-Khatib has strongly opposed the decision, both to the film’s producers and to the festival, and has made clear his wish for the film to remain in competition and be presented in Marrakech.
The withdrawal is related to the wider context of strained relations between Algeria and Morocco, in particular Morocco’s security and military ties with Israel.

In a statement (see below in full), Salad Issaad, the producer of Chronicles From The Siege and CEO of Isaad Film Production, said his company had initiated, financed and produced the film “out of a profound ethical commitment to the Palestinian cause, with the intention of bringing an independent, uncompromising, and politically engaged story to the screen.”

“We were deeply shocked by the official visit to Morocco on November 9 by senior representatives of the Israeli military, which is engaged in what we consider to be a genocidal war against the Palestinian people. This visit, which forms part of the strengthening of military cooperation between Morocco and Israel, represents, in our view, an intolerable contradiction of the values our film stands for.”
Isaad also cited the festival’s “direct institutional ties” to the ruling royal family.

He said the decision was made “entirely independently, without any external pressure, and rests solely with us as producers… This decision is ours alone, and everyone remains free tovmake their own choices according to their own conscience.”

The film’s surprise withdrawal comes despite it being linked to the festival for several years. In 2024, Chronicles From The Siege received support from the Atlas Workshops, Marrakech’s talent development programme for filmmakers and producers from Morocco, the Arab world and Africa. The film was awarded the Atlas Prize for post-production. Its selection for Marrakech’s official competition was confirmed on June 1.

Isaad said he would return the post-production award to the festival. He added that the decision to withdraw the film “in no way diminishes our appreciation for the festival’s artistic and operational teams, nor our deep respect for Moroccan artists and audiences, with whom we would have genuinely loved to share this film.”

Chronicles From The Siege centres on a group of ordinary people whose lives are turned upside down when their refugee camp is placed under siege. Five friends assemble at an abandoned video store, whose owner has struggled amid hunger and isolation, where their relationships are put to the test. Inspired by the director’s experiences during the siege of Yarmouk refugee camp in Syria, the film reflects the broader Palestinian experience of the past 70 years.
The cast is led by Nadeem Rimawi, Saja Kilani, Ahmad Kontar, Samer Bisharat and Ahmed Zitouni.
The film was initiated and produced by Salah Issaad of Algeria’s Issaad Film Productions, Taqiyeddine Issaad of France’s Evidence Film and co-produced by Sofiane Zermani of France’s 2 Princes Films.
International sales are handled by Paris-based Loco Films.
Marrakech film festival runs from November 20-28.
Statement by Salah Issaad on the withdrawal of Chronicles From The Siege from Marrakech

In accordance with our rights and responsibilities as producers, we have made the carefully considered decision to withdraw our film, Chronicles from the Siege, from the Marrakech International Film Festival.

We initiated, financed, and produced this film out of a profound ethical commitment to the Palestinian cause, with the intention of bringing an independent, uncompromising, and politically engaged story to the screen.

We were deeply shocked by the official visit to Morocco on November 9 by senior representatives of the Israeli military, which is engaged in what we consider to be a genocidal war against the Palestinian people. This visit, which forms part of the strengthening of military cooperation between Morocco and Israel, represents, in our view, an intolerable contradiction of the values our film stands for.

Unlike other international film festivals that operate independently of political authorities, the Marrakech International Film Festival maintains direct institutional ties to the Royal Palace. The festival is held under the High Patronage of the King, and its foundation is chaired by his brother.

Under these circumstances, we believe that maintaining our participation in an event so closely associated with the royal institutions would be incompatible with the convictions that inspired us to make this film in the first place.

This decision was made entirely independently, without any external pressure, and rests solely with us as producers. We stand by it fully, guided by our integrity and by the principles that led us to initiate, finance, and produce this film. This decision is ours alone, and everyone remains free to make their own choices according to their own conscience.

Furthermore, as our film received a post-production award at the Atlas Workshops in 2024, we have also decided to return the award to the festival. We sincerely thank the international jury that granted us this recognition for the trust and interest they showed in our project following the presentation we delivered alongside the director.

Finally, our withdrawal in no way diminishes our appreciation for the festival’s artistic and operational teams, nor our deep respect for Moroccan artists and audiences, with whom we would have genuinely loved to share this film.
